A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Intention-Conditioned Flow Occupancy Models, with 37 pages and complete appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on ExORL and OGBench in Figure 3 and Table 4, plus robotics evaluation and ablation results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains the original ExORL, OGBench and robotics experiments, together with the supplementary analyses and ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, lines 7–8, replaces intention z with Gaussian noise epsilon in the future-state interpolation and current-flow regression target. This locally corrects the stated computations to match the existing Equation 5 and Appendix A.3; it does not establish a change to the implemented method or a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ExORL, OGBench and RT-1/SimplerEnv coverage. Figure 20d corrects a task label to cube double task 1, which was already included in Appendix F.12 and the figure caption; no new task is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 4 and the appendix experiments, including the selected visual-task baselines, robotics baselines, alternative intention encoders and policy-extraction variants.

E3.justification: The dataset allocations, preprocessing, training budgets, evaluation metrics, checkpoint averaging and supplementary experimental protocols remain unchanged in Appendix D and Appendix F.

E4.justification: The intention-encoding, policy-extraction, reward-sparsity, dataset-size, dataset-quality and hyperparameter analyses are retained. Figure 20d corrects the label of an existing KL-regularization sweep without adding or changing the analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over eight seeds for state-based tasks and four for image-based tasks, including the four-seed robotics evaluation. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4, plotted values, error bars and stated findings are unchanged. Figure 20d corrects an existing panel's task label, consistent with the previously documented tasks and hyperparameters; it does not introduce different measured outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, flow-matching equations, ELBO and information-bottleneck derivations, and implicit-GPI analysis are unchanged. Algorithm 1's corrections align its pseudocode with existing mathematics without revising the theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning intention-conditioned occupancy modeling, implicit GPI and effective pre-training and fine-tuning.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning reward sparsity, latent intentions and Monte Carlo estimation remain unchanged. The limitation that consecutive state-action pairs may inadequately capture trajectory-level intentions is also retained.

D1.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1 removes implementation ambiguity between latent intentions and Gaussian flow noise, improving reproducibility guidance. Architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, training times and code-access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, bibliography and research positioning are unchanged, including the distinctions from prior TD flows, forward-backward representations and standard GPI.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 28 February 2026 to v4 dated 11 May 2026. The prose, terminology and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The third subplot in Figure 20d changes its task label from scene task 1 to cube double task 1, removing a duplicated scene label. Its bars, error bars and layout remain unchanged, as do the other figures and tables.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects two pseudocode errors that conflicted with the existing flow-matching equations and fixes a misleading task label in Figure 20d. These localized repairs improve internal consistency, implementation guidance and readability of the ablation evidence. The experiments, theoretical arguments and core claims remain unchanged.
